comments.author: Alex Warren
comments.content: Indeed, this is exactly the sort of thing I want to play around with in my own game, which is why Jimmy Maher's post resonated with me in particular. Just need to get on and write it!

comments.author: Jay Nabonne
comments.content:
The first article in particular touches on something I was toying with recently, and they it succinctly in the article - is it you making the actions in the game, such that the game is about the choices you're making, or are you stepping into the role of an actor in a story, such that you are no longer yourself as much as you are now looking through the eyes of someone else, someone who might not behave the way you would behave. It's a a bizarre thing to get your head around.

Here is an interesting thought (perhaps this has already been done): what if when you enter commands in the game, they are conceptually being transmitted to an in-game counterpart, someone with his/her own point of view and morals, someone who might take your command and twist it, someone who might just flat out say "no" to what you wish?
